zh.title: 達美航空見習副機師滑行中接電話據報遭解僱
zh.summary: 達美航空一名見習副機師據報在飛機滑行準備起飛時接聽手機，機長隨即返回登機門並將其請下飛機，該名副機師其後遭解僱；事件源自播客節目轉述，達美航空尚未證實，播客亦未提供航班編號與日期。
body: 據播客節目Black Box Aviation Podcast轉述，一名達美航空見習副機師在初始操作經驗（IOE）訓練期間執行首趟上線航班，飛機由亞特蘭大滑行準備起飛時，他的手機響起，他在機長滑行期間接聽了電話。機長隨即返回登機門，將該名副機師請下飛機，其後該名副機師遭到解僱。

滑行屬於飛行的關鍵階段：1981年實施的無菌駕駛艙規則、現行聯邦航空規則第121.542條，禁止機長允許任何可能分散機組注意力的活動，適用於滑行、起飛、降落及1萬英尺以下除巡航外的操作階段；2012年法案更明定第121部航空公司機組在值勤崗位使用個人裝置違法，2014年最終規則將禁令擴及所有飛行階段，並於2014年4月14日生效，相關修法部分源於美國國家運輸安全委員會在2009年科爾根航空事故後提出的建議。新進機師在初始操作經驗階段須在檢定機師督導下執行實際航班，Live And Let’s Fly認為訓練階段正是新進人員展現能否遵守程序的關鍵時刻。
這起事件目前仍未經證實。達美航空尚未證實相關說法，播客節目亦未提供航班編號或日期，因此無法確認事件發生的時間與經過是否如轉述所述；目前也沒有資料顯示美國聯邦航空總署已就此展開調查，或有達美航空的聲明與解僱紀錄。至於解僱決定本身，相關來源未說明該名副機師先前是否有其他紀錄、他向機長說了什麼，或達美航空試用期條款的內容。

en.title: Delta trainee pilot reportedly dismissed after answering phone while taxiing
en.summary: A Delta Air Lines first officer on new-hire training reportedly lost his job after answering his cellphone while the aircraft was taxiing for departure, according to an account shared on the Black Box Aviation Podcast. The captain is said to have returned to the gate and had the first officer removed; Delta has not confirmed the account.
body: A Delta Air Lines first officer on new-hire training reportedly lost his job after answering his cellphone while the aircraft was taxiing for departure, according to an account shared on the Black Box Aviation Podcast. The captain is said to have returned to the gate rather than continue to the runway, and the first officer was removed from the aircraft and later dismissed. The podcast's social post places the incident in Atlanta and calls it the new hire's first trip on the line.

"They were taxing out on his IOE ... and his phone rang. He answered, while the captain taxied," the Black Box Aviation Podcast reported. "Captain goes back to the gate, has him removed, and he got fired." Taxi is treated as a critical phase of flight: the 1981 sterile cockpit rule, now found in 14 CFR 121.542, bars the pilot in command from permitting any activity that could distract flight crew members during taxi, takeoff, landing, and other operations below 10,000 feet except cruise. Congress made personal device use at the duty station unlawful for Part 121 flight crew members in the Federal Aviation Administration's Modernization and Reform Act of 2012, and the 2014 final rule extended the prohibition on personal wireless devices to every phase of flight, taking effect on April 14, 2014. The rule was prompted in part by NTSB recommendations after the 2009 Colgan accident.

The account remains unverified, since Delta has not confirmed it and the podcast provided no flight number or date, leaving it unclear when the episode occurred and whether it unfolded as described. Nothing available yet shows an FAA investigation, a Delta statement, or a record of the dismissal. The dismissal itself is harder to assess, because the sources do not say whether the first officer had earlier concerns on record, what he told the captain, or what Delta's probationary terms provide. New hires complete Initial Operating Experience, flying actual trips under a check pilot, and Live And Let's Fly argues that training is precisely when a new hire should show he can be trusted to follow procedures.
